purpose: Refurbished high-memory Apple Silicon and legacy NVIDIA Volta hardware whose memory capacity, bandwidth, energy profile, or secondary-market pricing makes it relevant to local LLM inference.
notes: Apple Certified Refurbished prices are point-in-time configuration prices from Apple Canada; storage capacity can materially inflate a system price and should not be treated as a pure compute-price comparison.

Model-size practicality statements are conservative estimates based on memory capacity and common quantized-weight footprints; exact fit depends on runtime, context length, KV cache, model architecture and OS overhead.
Volta is a legacy CUDA target: CUDA 13 removed offline compilation and library support for Volta, so CUDA 12.x-era application stacks must be verified before purchase.

hardware.product: Mac Studio (2022) M1 Max 64GB - Apple Certified Refurbished

system_power_w.note: Apple wall-power reference is for a 32GB M1 Max Mac Studio; the 64GB refurb configuration may differ.

hardware.model_size_practicality: Estimate: strong fit for 7B-30B quantized models and many larger low-bit models; 64GB unified memory leaves less than the full nominal capacity available to model weights after macOS/runtime/KV-cache overhead.
hardware.off_grid_suitability: high for workstation-class inference; Apple documents about 11W idle and 115W maximum wall power for a reference M1 Max Mac Studio, substantially below many discrete-GPU workstations.

hardware.product: Mac Studio (2022) M1 Ultra - Apple Certified Refurbished

system_power_w.note: Apple wall-power reference is for M1 Ultra 48-core GPU / 64GB / 1TB; 128GB and 64-core-GPU configurations may differ.

hardware.model_size_practicality: Estimate: 64GB configurations are strong for 30B-class quantized models; 128GB configurations can hold many 70B-class quantized models with room for runtime/KV cache, subject to exact quantization, context and software overhead.
hardware.off_grid_suitability: medium-high for its memory bandwidth/capacity; Apple documents 13W idle and 215W maximum wall draw for a reference 64GB M1 Ultra system.

pricing.note: 128GB unified memory / 8TB SSD / 48-core GPU configuration; large SSD materially inflates price, so this is not a clean compute-only value comparison.

hardware.software_lifecycle_warning: NVIDIA lists Volta's last CUDA Toolkit support as CUDA 12.x and last driver branch as R580. CUDA 13 removed offline compilation and library support for Volta; verify application binaries and dependencies before purchase.
hardware.model_size_practicality: 32GB HBM2 can hold many 30B-class quantized models depending on context/runtime overhead. Its 900GB/s bandwidth is exceptional for the observed used price, but legacy software and 250W passive cooling materially increase operational friction.
quantization_compatibility: INT8 Tensor Core paths where supported by legacy-compatible runtimes
hardware.off_grid_suitability: low; 250W board power plus forced-air cooling offsets the excellent bandwidth-per-dollar.

pricing.note: US$645 listing localized to about CA$911.06 with free international shipping when indexed; taxes/import exposure and seller condition still apply.
